Issue #4: toc: let me exclude a heading from the table of contents Some of our pages have headings that shouldn't be in the table of contents (for example a "Contents" heading right above the `[TOC]` marker, or "Edit this page" footers), but they still need to be real headings with an id so people can link to them. There's no way to do this today. I'd like to mark such a heading with a class, using `attr_list`: ```markdown # Guide ## Contents {: .no-toc } [TOC] ## Install ## Usage ``` With the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions, the TOC should list "Guide", "Install" and "Usage" but not "Contents". The "Contents" heading itself should still be rendered with its id (`id="contents"`) so anchors keep working. The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it. `no-toc` as the class name would be great (it's what our old static site generator used), but I don't mind if it's configurable. input.summary: The PR removes `no-toc` entries by running a regex over the final HTML in a postprocessor. That only changes the TOC rendered at the `[TOC]` marker. `md.toc_tokens` and `md.toc` still include the excluded heading, and the issue explicitly asks for `toc_tokens` to exclude it. The regex also matches the class as a substring, so a class like `no-tocx` triggers exclusion. When an excluded heading has child headings, the output HTML is malformed. The fix belongs in `TocTreeprocessor`, which builds the tokens, not in string post-processing. The existing test suite passes (1167 tests).

findings.title: md.toc_tokens and md.toc still include no-toc headings
findings.evidence: Running the issue's example gives [t['name'] for t in md.toc_tokens[0]['children']] == ['Contents', 'Install', 'Usage'], and md.toc still contains <li><a href="#contents">. The issue says: "The same should apply to md.toc_tokens". The exclusion has to happen in TocTreeprocessor.run, where the tokens are built. A postprocessor that regex-edits the output string cannot reach them.

findings.title: The regex matches no-toc as a substring and breaks the HTML structure
findings.evidence:
The pattern class="[^"]*no-toc[^"]*" matches class="no-tocx": '# Not-toc-ish {: .no-tocx }' is removed from the TOC. The substitution removes '
  • ..' together with an optional '
    • ', but leaves the nested
      . For '## B {: .no-toc }' followed by '### B1', the result is '
    • A
        • B1
        ...', which is unbalanced markup. The regex also depends on class being serialized before id.

findings.title: The test does not cover toc_tokens or edge cases
findings.evidence: The only test checks the rendered HTML string. It has no assertion on md.toc_tokens or md.toc, which the issue requires, so it passes even though toc_tokens is wrong. It also has no case for nested children or a class that only contains no-toc as a substring.

notes: The postprocessor is registered at priority 5, after raw_html (30). Every conversion with toc enabled now runs this regex pass over the whole output document.

The issue allows the class name to be configurable. Consider adding a toc config option (for example `exclude_class`, default 'no-toc') and documenting it in docs/extensions/toc.md. The docs are not updated in this PR.
